# STMicroelectronics’ STM32H7P MCUs embed digital signal processing, edge-AI, and real-time control for demanding industrial applications


Nov 4, 2026 Geneva, Switzerland


- Enlarging STM32H7 series with enhanced DSP and edge-AI performance for embedded control, digital power, and sensing
- Dedicated DSP and neural-processing hardware accelerators, optimized memory, strong industrial peripheral set

STMicroelectronics’[STM32H7P microcontrollers](https://www.st.com/en/microcontrollers-microprocessors/stm32h7p4-p5.html?icmp=tt51485_gl_pron_oct2026) add hardware acceleration for DSP and edge AI workloads alongside a 2773-CoreMark® Arm® Cortex®-M7 to handle digital power, motor control, condition monitoring, and other mission-critical industrial applications.


The architecture includes ST’s Hardware Signal Processor (HSP) and Neural-ART ™ Neural Processing Unit (NPU). The HSP is a powerful, cost-optimized and energy-efficient DSP accelerator for matrix, vector, and digital signal processing operations. By offloading these workloads from the main CPU, HSP helps free up Cortex-M7 bandwidth and can reduce the need for a dedicated external DSP. It cuts the time for Fast Fourier Transforms (FFTs) by up to 5 times compared to software implementation on Cortex-M7.


*“The STM32H7P extends the proven STM32H7 series, with two dedicated hardware accelerators alongside a 520MHz Cortex-M7 core that deliver 1.7-times the performance of alternative products on the market. Combining more real-time performance with advanced hardware acceleration for DSP and edge-AI these MCUs let engineers build the next generation of smart, responsive embedded systems across industrial, power electronics, sensing, and intelligent edge applications,”* said Laurent Vera, STM32 Marketing Director, STMicroelectronics. *“In addition, richer analog and timer capabilities, and strong cost efficiency are ideal for power electronics applications such as solar, digital power, and motor control.”*


The new MCUs feature larger Tightly Coupled Memories (TCM) for fast access to instructions and data, maximizing the architecture’s performance in real-time control, signal processing, and AI inference.


For customers seeking a high-performance cost-optimized MCU, the new series offers up to 2MB of Flash for non-volatile code and data storage at a price point similar to the previous 1MB STM32H7 series, enabling general-purpose and mass-market designs to deliver more real-time performance and greater memory density without moving to a higher-cost platform.


In addition to its compute enhancements, the STM32H7P features advanced analog peripherals (ADC, DAC and comparators) and timers inherited from the newly introduced STM32G5 mixed-signal series, making it a compelling solution for control applications and strengthening industrial application development.


The Neural-ART NPU frees edge-AI workloads from software constraints, enhancing efficiency and allowing larger networks and more complex. Bringing up to 85 GOPS to the STM32H7P series, the NPU has already demonstrated 40-times faster inference than software running ST’s AI Arc Fault Circuit Interrupter (AFCI) model for solar- inverter safety. The anomaly detection model is shown to run 20 times faster, and the AI battery-management system (BMS) model runs 15 times faster.


ST’s Edge AI Suite provides a complete environment for embedded machine-learning development, with case studies and a set of tools and resources to help and accelerate the development and deployment of AI models on STM32. Developers can also take advantage of DSP enablement software and ST’s X-CUBE-MCSDK-2 motor-control software tools.


The STM32H7P will also connect with the upgraded STM32Cube ecosystem, including the enhanced STM32CubeMX2 configurator and also the latest code-size optimized hardware abstraction layer, HAL2.


Ready for demanding industrial environments, the STM32H7P MCUs operate up to 125°C ambient temperature and are included in ST’s industrial longevity support program. An exposed-pad LQFP package option further enhances thermal dissipation, supporting robust operation in high-temperature industrial designs.


The STM32H7P series is sampling at OEMs now, with production planned in January 2027, priced from $4.43 with 1MB Flash in LQFP100 package, for orders of 10,000 units. The NUCLEO-H7P5II evaluation board and STM32H7P5IDK Discovery kit will also be available in January 2027.


Visit[www.st.com/stm32h7p](https://www.st.com/en/microcontrollers-microprocessors/stm32h7p4-p5.html?icmp=tt51485_gl_pron_oct2026) for more information.
